solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Box, consumed by booze, with right arm

indicators.note: something consumed by another is swallowed inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: wine is a kind of booze
a chest is a box

explanation.surface: A boxer has had a drink and swings a right arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' and 'right arm' suggest boxing, but 'arm' alone is the definition: a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A Winchester is a famous make of rifle, and a firearm is an arm in the weapon sense.

clue.text: Glasgow's latest amateur band

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its final one, here the end of Glasgow's

parts.note: a ham is an amateur, especially a radio enthusiast or poor actor

explanation.surface: The newest amateur group to come out of Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Wham! was a 1980s British pop duo, so the name of a music group.

clue.text: Heavenly body training on bend in English river

indicators.note: the training-on-bend pieces sit inside the river's name

parts.note: the Nene is a river in eastern England
PT is physical training
a U-bend is a pipe bend, giving U

explanation.surface: A celestial object exercising on a curve of an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue places PT above U.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is a planet, and planets are heavenly bodies.

clue.text: Male and female from tiny island designed period hat

parts.note: Herm is a small Channel Island near Guernsey

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters of period hat are newly arranged

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Men's and women's fashion: a period hat made on a small island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' turns PERIOD HAT into APHRODITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermaphrodite has both male and female sexual organs.

clue.text: Exhibition site disturbs the main orator

indicators.note: the exhibition site breaks into the sea, interrupting it

parts.note: the main is an old poetic term for the open sea
the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham

explanation.surface: A show at a venue upsets the main speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' looks like an adjective-plus-noun phrase about the chief orator, but it means the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger was a Roman philosopher and rhetorician famed as a speaker.

clue.text: Untidy notes hamper this person on special school course

indicators.note: to hamper is to hold in, so one piece is enclosed by the anagrammed letters
untidy signals the letters of notes are messed up

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as this person, giving me

explanation.surface: A messy set of notes holds up this pupil on a particular school course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school course' reads like a curriculum, but it is a pudding named after a school; 'on' simply sets the special letter at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton mess, a dessert of meringue, strawberries and cream named after Eton College, is a course of a meal linked to a school.

clue.text: Lacking electronics, correspond with one Asian city

indicators.note: lacking means doing without, so letters are dropped from the verb

parts.note: to correspond is to agree or match
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Without electronic gear, you write to a single city in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'electronics' stands for two E's (E for electronic, made plural), both of which leave AGREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a city in northern India, home of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Tradesman beginning to grow more work-shy

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of grow

parts.note: lazier means more averse to work

explanation.surface: A worker who starts becoming less keen to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier is a tradesman who fits glass in windows.

clue.text: Military officer declined idea to promote staff in data processing

indicators.note: declined here means bent out of shape, so the letters of idea are rearranged
the staff word sits inside the abbreviation for data processing
in a down clue promoting a word raises it, so it reads upwards

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff

explanation.surface: An officer turned down a plan to advance staff working in computing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to promote' raises a word, so it reads bottom to top; 'declined' is bent out of shape rather than refused.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is an officer acting as personal assistant to a senior commander.

clue.text: Patient, regularly ingesting opposite, splits drug

indicators.note: ingesting means taking in, so the reversed word goes inside
taking letters at regular intervals from Patient: the 2nd, 4th and 6th
going the opposite way means reading backwards

parts.note: rips means splits or tears

explanation.surface: A patient regularly taking something opposing splits a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks AIN from Patient; 'opposite' reverses RIPS to SPIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling medicine.

clue.text: Vigilant head of army invades foreign ground

indicators.note: the army's head goes into the rearranged ground
foreign suggests something altered or strange, so the letters of ground are mixed
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An alert general leads an invasion of overseas territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' mixes GROUND to ONGURD, into which A goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on guard means watchful and alert to danger.

clue.text: Toothless creature entertaining at a complex, in shifts

indicators.note: complex signals a tangled arrangement of the letters
when in shifts it moves away, leaving the remaining letters

parts.note: taken as written, the letter pool
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A toothless animal performs at a complex, working in shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I and N from ENTERTAINING AT A and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant anteater has no teeth, using its long tongue to eat ants and termites.

clue.text: University professor's first to enter non-academic building alone

indicators.note: the professor's initial goes into the rearranged letters
building suggests constructing the letters into a new shape
first means the opening letter of professor's

explanation.surface: A university professor enters a non-academic building on his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a noun but rearranges NON-ACADEMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaccompanied means without company, solo.

clue.text: Associate on the wagon saw villain driving

parts.note: on the wagon means abstaining from drink, teetotal, abbreviated TT
to hew is to cut, as with a saw
a heel is a cad or villain

explanation.surface: A teetotal colleague spotted a crook in charge of a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the past of see but is the verb to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at the wheel means steering a vehicle, that is driving.

clue.text: Note Ethel, hiding what babies naturally do

indicators.note: Note Ethel conceals the run of letters within it

explanation.surface: Ethel is told about a natural stage of infancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies grow their first teeth as a normal stage of development.

clue.text: Morecambe welcomes such extremists in the occult

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so letters go inside the comedian's first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a famous British comedian
so can mean such, as in 'so much'

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here of the

explanation.surface: A seaside town takes in extremists dabbling in the occult.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a Lancashire resort, but here it is the comedian Eric Morecambe, whose first name opens up after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric and occult both describe secret knowledge understood only by initiates.

clue.text: Constant sharpness about curry-house's latest dish

parts.note: K is a symbol for a constant in science
edge means sharpness, as of a blade or tongue
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the latest letter is the final one

explanation.surface: Persistent tang surrounds the newest dish from an Indian restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is a dish of rice, smoked fish and eggs, Anglo-Indian in origin.

clue.text: Some of water extremely hazy — doctor round with details

indicators.note: taking the extremes of hazy, its first and last letters

parts.note: O is round in shape
gen is informal British for information or details

explanation.surface: Murky water, and a doctor going round with the particulars.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is H2O, so this gas is a component of every water molecule.

clue.text: Director on Tate's east wing, in review of Hirst, cannot decide

indicators.note: a review goes over things again, so these letters are reconsidered and rearranged
the east wing of a word written left to right is its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gallery boss reviewing Damien Hirst's work at the Tate is undecided.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate is the London gallery and Damien Hirst a British artist; E plus HIRST is rearranged to ITHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hesitates and wavers is unable to make up their mind.

clue.text: Old monastic manuscript, about the French, not available for restoration

indicators.note: restoring sends things back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
the manuscript abbreviation goes around the French article

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: An ancient monastery manuscript in French is not available to be restored.
explanation.walkthrough: MLES plus NA is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: St Anselm was an 11th-century Benedictine monk and Archbishop of Canterbury.

clue.text: Lace ten jars with alcohol

indicators.note: jars as a verb means jolts, so the letters of ten are shaken up

parts.note: wine is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Ten jars spiked with drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jars' looks like containers but is the verb meaning jolts.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace is to weave or twist together, as laces are threaded.

clue.text: Camp volunteers left trapped by sink

indicators.note: the volunteers and left are held within the word for sink

parts.note: to sag is to sink or droop
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers abandoned at a camp, stuck by the kitchen sink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp.

clue.text: Scottish engineer catches fish with palm? An ancient way

indicators.note: the engineer's name catches the other pieces inside it

parts.note: James Watt was a Scottish engineer famous for steam engines
ling are fish of the cod family, here plural
a palm is an example of a tree, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A Scots engineer lands fish, holding a palm leaf, on an old road.
explanation.walkthrough: Watling Street is a Roman road across England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Roman road from Dover through London to Wroxeter is a very old route.

clue.text: Jewellery, for example, reflected on department store

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: M&S is Marks & Spencer, a British department store chain

explanation.surface: Jewellery, say, displayed in a mirror at a department store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' looks like a link but gives EG, turned to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gems are precious stones, worn as jewellery.

clue.text: Perhaps contacts unknown member of the flock occupying organ

indicators.note: the unknown and sheep occupy the space inside the organ

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
Y is a mathematical unknown
a ewe is a female sheep in a flock

explanation.surface: Maybe acquaintances: an unknown churchgoer sitting at the organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contacts' suggests acquaintances and 'flock' a congregation, but they mean lenses and sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact lenses are an example of things worn on the eyes for vision.

clue.text: Can business imports corrupt art?

indicators.note: importing brings something inside, so the scrambled letters enter

parts.note: a line is a line of business, a trade

indicators.note: corrupt suggests the letters of art are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Can a firm that imports goods corrupt art?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb opening a question, but is the slang noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang, especially American, for a toilet.

clue.text: Destructive bed-hopper? Old Conservative oozes sensuality

indicators.note: oozing lets something leak out, so these letters are lost

parts.note: a locust hops through flower beds and crops, destroying them
O is old and C is Conservative, both standard abbreviations

explanation.surface: A philanderer, an old Tory, exuding sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed-hopper' suggests a philanderer but means an insect in garden beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lust is strong sexual desire, closely tied to sensuality.

clue.text: Daughter, during Rag Week, attacked with poles a London landmark

indicators.note: the daughter appears during, that is within, the other letters
attacked suggests the letters are set upon and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; a rag week is a British student charity week
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: During a student charity week, a daughter attacked a famous London site with poles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew in west London are a well-known attraction.
